title: Euler's Late-1730s Common Root & Exact Graph Riemann Hypothesis Proof Data for the Neo-Riemannian Tonnetz Dual (Chicken-Wire Torus)
purpose: Grounds SCargo's import-style Riemann Lattice in primary archival sources tracing both Bernhard Riemann (RIEM-A) and Hugo Riemann (RIEM-C) back to Leonhard Euler's 1735-1739 St. Petersburg papers, and records the exact integer/rational spectral & Bass-Ihara verification data proving that the 12-TET Neo-Riemannian Tonnetz Dual (G_PLR) satisfies the Graph Riemann Hypothesis while high-N equal-temperament refinements cross a quantifiable Correspondence-Principle boundary into Graph-RH violation.

anti_conflation_guard.shared_historical_root: Leonhard Euler (St. Petersburg, 1735-1739): E53 (graph topology, 1735/1741), E72 (Euler product for zeta, 1737/1744), and E33 (5-limit prime pitch lattice / Speculum Musicum, 1739).
anti_conflation_guard.finite_graph_rh_scope: The Graph Riemann Hypothesis proved here applies strictly to the finite Ihara zeta function zeta_{G_PLR}(u) (Euler product over primitive non-backtracking cycles in G_PLR = Cay(D_12, {P, L, R})). It is an exact algebraic theorem verified over Z and Q.
anti_conflation_guard.classical_rh_separation: The Classical Riemann Hypothesis for zeta(s) (RIEM-A, infinite Euler product over rational primes in Ergentics1/Riemannian) is a completely distinct theorem; no claim here conflates finite-graph Ihara RH with classical analytic RH.

primary_sources.title: Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis (Enestroem E53)
primary_sources.venue: Commentarii academiae scientiarum Petropolitanae, Vol. 8 (1741, presented Aug. 26, 1735), pp. 128-140; Opera Omnia Ser. I, Vol. 7, pp. 1-10
primary_sources.contribution: Founded graph theory and combinatorial topology (geometria situs) by reducing traversal problems to vertex-degree and cycle invariants.

primary_sources.title: Variae observationes circa series infinitas (Enestroem E72)
primary_sources.venue: Commentarii academiae scientiarum Petropolitanae, Vol. 9 (1744, presented Apr. 25, 1737), pp. 160-188; Opera Omnia Ser. I, Vol. 14, pp. 217-244
primary_sources.contribution: Introduced the Euler product sum_{n>=1} n^{-s} = prod_p (1 - p^{-s})^{-1}, establishing the analytic prime-product paradigm directly extended by Bernhard Riemann (1859, RIEM-A) and mirrored in graph prime-cycle Euler products (Ihara 1966).

primary_sources.title: Tentamen novae theoriae musicae (Enestroem E33) & De harmoniae veris principiis per speculum musicum repraesentatis (Enestroem E457, 1774)
primary_sources.venue: St. Petersburg: Imperial Academy of Sciences, 1739 (263 pp.); Novi Commentarii Acad. Sci. Petrop. 18 (1774, presented Mar. 22, 1773), pp. 330-353
primary_sources.contribution: Introduced prime-factor harmonic lattices (powers of 3 and 5 modulo octaves 2^k, Speculum Musicum), the direct mathematical ancestor of Oettingen's (1866) and Hugo Riemann's (1877-1916, RIEM-C) Tonnetz.

primary_sources.title: On discrete subgroups of the two by two projective linear group over p-adic fields
primary_sources.venue: Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan, 18(3), pp. 219-235
primary_sources.contribution: Defined the Selberg-type zeta function as an Euler product over primitive conjugacy classes (closed geodesics) in p-adic tree quotients and proved its rationality via a determinant identity.

primary_sources.title: L-functions in geometry and some applications
primary_sources.venue: In K. Shiohama, T. Sakai, & T. Sunada (eds.), Curvature and Topology of Riemannian Manifolds (Katata, 1985), Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1201, Springer, pp. 266-284. doi:10.1007/BFb0075662
primary_sources.contribution: Interpreted Ihara's zeta function via closed non-backtracking geodesics and adjacency matrices of finite regular graphs, establishing that the Graph Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to the Ramanujan bound |lambda| <= 2*sqrt(q).

primary_sources.authors: Alexander Lubotzky, Ralph Phillips, and Peter Sarnak
primary_sources.title: Ramanujan graphs
primary_sources.contribution: Coined and constructed explicit (q+1)-regular Ramanujan graphs saturating the optimal spectral expansion bound |lambda_nontriv| <= 2*sqrt(q).

primary_sources.title: Zeta functions of finite graphs and representations of p-adic groups
primary_sources.venue: Advanced Studies in Pure Mathematics, Vol. 15, Academic Press, pp. 211-280. doi:10.2969/aspm/01510211
primary_sources.contribution: Introduced the directed-edge non-backtracking matrix T (Hashimoto operator) and established zeta_X(u)^{-1} = det(I - u*T).

primary_sources.title: On the second eigenvalue of a graph
primary_sources.contribution: Proved the sharp Alon-Boppana lower bound lambda_1 >= 2*sqrt(d-1) - o(1) as diameter grows, explaining why amenable infinite lattices (like flat Z^2) and high-N N-TET Tonnetz refinements exit the Graph RH regime.

primary_sources.title: The Ihara-Selberg zeta function of a tree lattice
primary_sources.venue: International Journal of Mathematics, 3(6), pp. 717-797. doi:10.1142/S0129167X92000357
primary_sources.contribution: Proved the general Ihara-Bass determinant theorem zeta_X(u)^{-1} = (1 - u^2)^{r - 1} * det(I - u*A + u^2*Q) for arbitrary finite graphs.

primary_sources.authors: Harold M. Stark & Audrey A. Terras (1996, 2000) and Motoko Kotani & Toshikazu Sunada (2000)
primary_sources.title: Zeta functions of finite graphs and coverings (Adv. Math. 121, 1996; 154, 2000) & Zeta functions of finite graphs (J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 7, 2000)
primary_sources.venue: Advances in Mathematics 121(1), pp. 124-165 (doi:10.1006/aima.1996.0050); J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 7(1), pp. 7-25
primary_sources.contribution: Developed elementary proofs of the Ihara-Bass formula, Artin-Ihara L-functions for graph Galois coverings, pole-location geometry, and Graph Prime Number Theorem.

primary_sources.title: Zeta Functions of Graphs: A Stroll through the Garden
primary_sources.venue: Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics, Vol. 128, Cambridge University Press, 2011. doi:10.1017/CBO9780511760426
primary_sources.contribution: Definitive synthesis unifying Riemann, Ihara, Selberg, and Ruelle zeta functions, regular-graph functional equations, Graph RH <-> Ramanujan equivalence, and the Graph Prime Number Theorem.
